title: DDIA 12 · THE FUTURE OF DATA SYSTEMS
subtitle: The book's conclusion: there is no one database that does everything. Build systems as a source of truth plus derived views connected by logs.
footer: Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann). Read the book.

blocks.text: Every other store is a derived view, like an index or materialized view, except in separate specialized systems. Any view can be dropped and rebuilt by replaying the log.
Kappa: one streaming codebase. To fix a bug or change logic, start v2 reading the log from the beginning, let it catch up, and switch reads over.
The duplicate hits the unique constraint, and the server returns the original result. Only an end-to-end ID from the origin catches every duplicate.

head: Timeliness
Integrity
rows: No corruption: no lost or double money, no contradictions
Room sold twice; card charged twice
Idempotency, unique constraints, atomic log append, reconciliation

items: "How do you guarantee no double charge?"
Client idempotency key + unique constraint + the payment provider's idempotency + a daily reconciliation job against provider settlement files.
"Search is a derived view. Timeliness can lag seconds; the checkout price is read from the source of truth (integrity)."
"How would you change the aggregation logic?"
Kappa: deploy v2 consumer from offset 0 to a new table, compare, switch.

blocks.text: "I separate integrity from timeliness: money and inventory are strongly consistent and audited; everything the user browses is a derived, eventually consistent view."
